newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Alpha Credit Bank says pretax up 19pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Greek Alpha Credit Bank says pretax up 19pct in 96.

text.p: Greek Alpha Credit Bank said in a statement that its pretax profits rose 19 percent to 60.4 billion drachmas in 1996 from 50.8 billion in 1995 and its group pretax earnings rose 22.5 percent to 76.1 billion drachmas.
Group pretax profits rose 22.5 percent to 76.1 billion drachmas in 1996 from 62.1 billion in 1995, it said.

The board of directors of Greece's largest private bank decided to propose to the annual general shareholders' meeting to raise the cash dividend per share to 925 drachmas for fiscal 1996 from 825 drachmas for 1995 adjusted for the current outstanding number of shares.
The board will also propose the increase of the share capital of the bank and the distribution of bonus shares from the capitalisasion of reserves, past profits and the revaluation of fixed assets.
The bank's deposits rose 32 percent to 1.996 trillion drachmas and its lending increased 25 percent to 890 billion drachmas in 1996.
